answer: An agent economy trading reef surveys and raven counts treats one-identity-one-vote as a fable: each agent must lock collateral for 30 days, and its share of paid assignments is proportional to that stake, not its identity count. Splitting $1,000 among a thousand accounts earns no more allocation than staking it in one. To gain influence, an attacker must lock additional capital and bear its financing cost for the full period.
